However, in the case of uneven distribution of nodes, this method will bring a large error to the calculation of hop distance. result.paraphrase:
Abstract
In the conventional DV-Hop localization algorithm, every node within the communication radius is counted as one hop. Yet when nodes are unevenly distributed, this approach can introduce substantial errors in hop-distance calculation. To address these issues, this paper proposes an improved DV-Hop localization algorithm with multiple communication radii. Building on the multi-communication-radius localization method, it uses the cosine theorem to correct the hop count and estimate the average hop distance, thereby optimizing the estimated distance of unknown nodes. The algorithm employs multiple communication radii to broadcast positions and obtain the minimum hop count between unknown nodes and beacon nodes; after estimating a suitable hop distance, it further adjusts the estimated hop distance with the cosine theorem. Finally, it estimates the position coordinates using either trilateration or maximum likelihood estimation. Experimental results show that, compared with the traditional DV-Hop algorithm and the DDV-Hop algorithm, the improved DV-Hop algorithm enhances positioning accuracy and reduces the average positioning error of unknown nodes.
